chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to us, from al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Faddal, from 'Ali b. 'Uqba, from Muyassir. He said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever attends the funeral of a Muslim, on the Day of Resurrection, he will be given four intercessions. He will not say a thing except that the angel will say: 'And for you is something like that.'

key_terms.الْمَلَكُ: The angel - a celestial being assigned to respond to the attendee's prayers
key_terms.شَفَاعَاتٍ: Intercessions - the ability to intercede on behalf of others before Allah
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: Day of Resurrection - the day of final judgment

ai.seo_question: What reward does Imam al-Baqir promise for attending the funeral of a Muslim?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir teaches that attending a Muslim's funeral earns the attendee four intercessions on the Day of Judgment, and that an angel will reciprocate every good prayer the attendee makes with a similar blessing for them. This encourages Muslims to support each other even in death, showing how communal acts of piety are rewarded with divine generosity that multiplies every good wish uttered during the funeral.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Faddal from `Ali b. `Uqba from Muyassir.  He said: I heard Aba Ja`far al-Baqir (as) say:
Whoever attends the funeral of a Muslim, on the Day of Resurrection, he will be given four intercessions. He will not say a thing except that the angel will say: “And for you is something like that.”
